observations.text: SP flew the Chandelle to the block MIF of (0) on this introduction sortie, following the IP's demonstration and directed inputs through the pitch and bank sequence. Bank and recovery heading were held only while the IP called the roll-out point, which is the expected standard for this stage of the block. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent control of the entry parameters is expected to improve.

SP required no control input from the IP on this introduction sortie and flew the Chandelle to completion after verbal prompts only. Bank was held within 20 degrees of the briefed value and the roll-out was 20 degrees off the reciprocal heading, with recognition delayed but the recovery flown by SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Chandelle without any IP intervention, establishing the briefed bank in the first 90 degrees of turn and holding a constant pitch attitude through the second. Deviations were limited to 14 degrees of bank and 13 degrees of recovery heading, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Chandelle accurately and without hesitation, using the outside reference line throughout and controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid way with no approach to stall. Recovery airspeed was within 7 knots of the briefed value and the roll-out within 8 degrees of the reciprocal heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Chandelle with exceptional precision on the first attempt, holding the briefed bank through the first 90 degrees and a constant pitch attitude through the second. Recovery airspeed was within 3 knots of the briefed value and the roll-out within 2 degrees of the reciprocal heading, with no IP input at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standard entry technique, did not establish the briefed 30 degrees of bank before starting the pitch increase in the Chandelle, and did not maintain the constant pitch attitude through the second 90 degrees of turn. Bank varied by 28 degrees and the roll-out was completed 32 degrees off the reciprocal heading, with the result that the IP directed the pitch and bank inputs and flew the recovery. Additional study of the Chandelle procedure in the Techniques and Procedures Manual is required.

SP completed the Chandelle within the desired standards for the block, controlling the A/C without an approach to stall at the completion point. The roll-out was made 20 degrees off the reciprocal heading and entry airspeed was 15 knots above the briefed value, both corrected after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition of the deviations was delayed on two of three repetitions. Marginal performance for the Training Section - self-recognition of the entry parameters is expected to improve.

SP flew the Chandelle without the IP's verbal prompts or intervention, following the standardized entry, pitch and roll-out sequence. Bank deviated by 15 degrees at the 90 degree point and recovery airspeed by 12 knots, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner by SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed the Chandelle to the standardized procedure with accuracy and speed, keeping the outside reference line in use for the entry and the roll-out point. Recovery heading was within 6 degrees of the reciprocal and recovery airspeed within 8 knots of the briefed value, with no IP prompting required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Chandelle with exceptional accuracy, controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid way with no approach to stall at the completion point. Bank was held within 2 degrees of the briefed value and the roll-out within 3 degrees of the reciprocal heading, with recovery airspeed within 2 knots. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a startle response that displaced the memorised recovery sequence when the stall warning activated near the completion point, did not maintain smooth and solid control of the A/C through the second 90 degrees of the Chandelle. Recovery airspeed fell 17 knots below the briefed value and the roll-out finished 30 degrees off the reciprocal heading, with the result that the IP took the controls to prevent an approach to stall.

SP, due to a late and uncoordinated roll-out input, did not complete the Chandelle with the wings level at the 180 degree point as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual. Recovery heading was 20 degrees off the reciprocal and entry airspeed was 15 knots above the briefed value, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition of the deviation was delayed.

SP flew the Chandelle within the desired standards, controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid way without an approach to stall. Bank exceeded the briefed value by 17 degrees at the 90 degree point and recovery heading was 16 degrees off the reciprocal on two repetitions, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency of bank control through the first 90 degrees is expected to improve.

SP flew the Chandelle accurately and promptly, without the IP's intervention, establishing the briefed bank in the first 90 degrees and holding a constant pitch attitude through the second. Recovery airspeed was within 8 knots of the briefed value and the roll-out within 7 degrees of the reciprocal heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew three consecutive Chandelles with exceptional accuracy, each entered on the briefed outside reference line and completed with the wings level at the 180 degree point. Deviations did not exceed 3 knots of airspeed and 2 degrees of recovery heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to overconfidence in the margin available at that airspeed and bank, entered the Chandelle without checking the entry parameters and allowed the bank to increase past the briefed value while the pitch attitude was still rising. Bank reached 32 degrees beyond the briefed value and the A/C entered the stall buffet before the 180 degree point, with the result that the IP took control and completed the recovery. The maneuver was not completed by SP without assistance.

SP, due to an insufficient rate of pitch increase in the first 90 degrees of turn, did not arrive at the maximum pitch attitude at the 90 degree point of the Chandelle. Recovery airspeed ended 10 knots below the briefed value and the roll-out was 20 degrees off the reciprocal heading, with the deviation corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition and correction were delayed.

SP, due to an absent cross-check of aircraft state against the primary flight instruments while working the outside reference line, did not hold the briefed bank through the first 90 degrees of the Chandelle. Bank varied by 15 degrees and recovery airspeed was 8 knots below the briefed value, both deviations recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP flew the Chandelle accurately and without delay, using the outside reference line for the entry and for the roll-out point. Deviations remained inside the desired criteria, with recovery airspeed 9 knots above the briefed value and the roll-out 9 degrees off the reciprocal heading. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter control of the recovery parameters is expected to improve with repetition.

SP flew the Chandelle above the desired standard, with a smooth and solid pitch and bank sequence and no approach to stall at the completion point. Recovery airspeed was within 2 knots of the briefed value, bank within 2 degrees and the roll-out within 3 degrees of the reciprocal heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Lazy Eight to the block MIF of (0) on the introduction sortie, following the IP's demonstration and directed inputs at the 45 and 90 degree points. Pitch and bank were coordinated only while the IP called the reference points, which is the expected standard for this stage of the block. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent use of the outside reference line is expected to improve.

SP flew the Lazy Eight to completion on the introduction sortie with the IP's verbal prompts only and no control input from the front cockpit. Bank was held within 20 degrees of the briefed value at the 90 degree point and the completion heading within 20 degrees of the section line. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Lazy Eight without any prompting or intervention from the IP, achieving the maximum pitch attitude at the 45 degree point and the maximum bank at the 90 degree point. Deviations were limited to 15 degrees of bank and 12 knots of completion airspeed, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Lazy Eight accurately and promptly, holding a constant rate of change of pitch and bank and controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid way with no approach to stall. Completion airspeed was within 8 knots of the briefed value and the roll-out within 7 degrees of the section line. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Lazy Eight with exceptional accuracy on the introduction sortie, with the two halves symmetrical about the section line and the wings level exactly at the 180 degree point. Bank was within 3 degrees of the briefed value and completion airspeed within 2 knots. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to incomplete knowledge of the limits applicable to the maneuver, did not fly the Lazy Eight as the symmetrical pair of climbing and descending turns described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, and did not reach the maximum pitch attitude at the 45 degree point. Bank at the 90 degree point exceeded the briefed value by 30 degrees and the completion heading was 28 degrees off the section line, with the result that the IP directed the pitch and bank inputs and flew the second half of the maneuver.

SP completed the Lazy Eight within the desired standards for the block, controlling the A/C without an approach to stall over the top. Bank at the 90 degree point was 20 degrees off the briefed value and completion airspeed was 10 knots below it, corrected after the IP's verbal prompts on each repetition. Marginal performance for the Training Section - recognition of the pitch and bank deviations without prompting is expected to improve.

SP flew the Lazy Eight without verbal prompts or intervention from the IP, following the standardized pitch and bank sequence throughout. Bank at the 90 degree point deviated by 14 degrees and completion airspeed by 12 knots, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner by SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed the Lazy Eight accurately and without hesitation, using the outside reference line to set the 45, 90 and 180 degree points. Bank was within 8 degrees of the briefed value and completion airspeed within 7 knots, with no IP prompting required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Lazy Eight with exceptional precision, maintaining a constant rate of change of pitch and bank through both halves without any approach to stall. Completion airspeed was within 3 knots of the briefed value and the roll-out within 2 degrees of the section line. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an abrupt and non-constant rate of pitch change through the first quadrant, did not achieve the maximum pitch attitude at the 45 degree point of the Lazy Eight and did not arrive wings level at the 180 degree point. Airspeed at the completion point was 18 knots below the briefed value with the stall warning active, with the result that the IP took the controls and recovered the A/C to level flight. The Lazy Eight sequence requires further ground review before the next sortie.

SP, due to an absent cross-check of aircraft state against the primary flight instruments during the descending half, did not fly the two halves of the Lazy Eight symmetrically about the section line. Bank at the 90 degree point was 20 degrees off the briefed value and completion airspeed was 15 knots above the briefed value, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition of the asymmetry was delayed until the second repetition.

SP flew the Lazy Eight within the desired standards, keeping the two halves recognizably symmetrical about the section line. Bank at the 90 degree point deviated by 17 degrees and completion airspeed by 13 knots above the briefed value, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency of the rate of pitch change through the first quadrant is expected to improve.

SP flew the Lazy Eight accurately and promptly without the IP's intervention, with the maximum pitch attitude set at the 45 degree point and the maximum bank at the 90 degree point. Deviations did not exceed 8 degrees of bank and 6 knots of completion airspeed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew consecutive Lazy Eights with exceptional accuracy, each pair of halves symmetrical about the same section line. Bank was within 2 degrees of the briefed value and completion airspeed within 3 knots, with the wings level at the 180 degree point on every repetition. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standard entry with the reference line not established before the pull, did not fly the Lazy Eight about a fixed outside reference and did not control the A/C in a smooth and solid way over the top of the first climbing turn. Bank varied by 35 degrees between the two halves and the A/C entered the stall buffet at the second 45 degree point, with the result that the IP took control and recovered the maneuver. The maneuver was not completed by SP without assistance.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated all cockpit workload inside the turn, did not maintain the constant rate of change of pitch and bank required through the Lazy Eight. Completion airspeed was 10 knots below the briefed value and the roll-out was 20 degrees off the section line, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition and correction were delayed.

SP, due to a slightly late roll input on the descending half, did not arrive with the wings level exactly at the 180 degree point of the Lazy Eight. Bank at the 90 degree point deviated by 14 degrees and the completion heading by 15 degrees from the section line, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP flew the Lazy Eight accurately and without delay, using the section line for both halves of the maneuver. Deviations stayed inside the desired criteria, with bank 9 degrees off the briefed value at the 90 degree point and completion airspeed 9 knots above the briefed value. Marginal performance for the Training Section - symmetry between the climbing and descending halves is expected to improve with repetition.

SP flew the Lazy Eight above the desired standard, with a constant rate of change of pitch and bank and smooth, solid control throughout. Completion heading was within 2 degrees of the section line, bank within 3 degrees of the briefed value and airspeed within 2 knots. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Aileron Roll to the block MIF of (0) on the introduction sortie, with the IP setting the entry pitch attitude and calling the roll input. The rate of roll was controlled only while directed from the front cockpit, which is the expected standard at this stage of the block. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent setting of the entry parameters is expected to improve.

SP flew the Aileron Roll to completion on the introduction sortie after the IP's verbal prompts only, with no control input from the front cockpit. The roll finished 20 degrees off the entry heading with recovery airspeed 15 knots above the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Aileron Roll without prompting or intervention from the IP, setting the briefed nose position above the horizon and rolling about the longitudinal axis. The roll finished 14 degrees off the entry heading and recovery airspeed reached 12 knots above the briefed value, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Aileron Roll accurately and promptly, holding a constant rate of roll and using the outside reference line throughout. The roll finished within 7 degrees of the entry heading and recovery airspeed within 8 knots of the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Aileron Roll with exceptional precision on the introduction sortie, with no pitch input during the roll and the longitudinal axis held on the reference line. The roll finished within 2 degrees of the entry heading and recovery airspeed within 3 knots of the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standard entry with the nose not raised to the briefed pitch attitude above the horizon, did not fly the Aileron Roll as a constant rate roll about the longitudinal axis. The roll finished 30 degrees off the entry heading with recovery airspeed 25 knots above the briefed value, with the result that the IP directed the entry and flew the recovery to level flight.

SP completed the Aileron Roll within the desired standards for the block, holding the longitudinal axis on the outside reference for most of the roll. The roll finished 20 degrees off the entry heading with recovery airspeed 15 knots above the briefed value, corrected after the IP's verbal prompts. Marginal performance for the Training Section - recognition of the heading deviation without prompting is expected to improve.

SP flew the Aileron Roll without the IP's verbal prompts, following the standardized entry and roll sequence. The roll finished 15 degrees off the entry heading and recovery airspeed reached 12 knots above the briefed value, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner by SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed the Aileron Roll to the standardized procedure with accuracy and speed, holding the briefed pitch attitude and a constant rate of roll. Recovery heading was within 8 degrees of the entry heading and recovery airspeed within 6 knots of the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Aileron Roll with exceptional accuracy, keeping the longitudinal axis fixed on the outside reference from entry to recovery. The roll finished within 3 degrees of the entry heading with recovery airspeed within 2 knots of the briefed value and no IP prompting at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an over-controlled aircraft (AE104) in the correction, applied pitch input during the roll instead of holding the longitudinal axis fixed on the outside reference. The nose dropped well through the horizon, recovery airspeed reached 28 knots above the briefed value and the roll finished 32 degrees off the entry heading, with the result that the IP took control and recovered the A/C.

SP, due to an inconsistent aileron input that did not produce a constant rate of roll, did not complete the Aileron Roll on the entry heading as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual. Recovery heading was 20 degrees off the entry heading and recovery airspeed 15 knots above the briefed value, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition of the deviation was delayed until the roll was complete.

SP flew the Aileron Roll within the desired standards, controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid way with a near constant rate of roll. The roll finished 16 degrees off the entry heading on two of three repetitions and recovery airspeed reached 13 knots above the briefed value, each deviation recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency of the entry pitch attitude is expected to improve.

SP flew the Aileron Roll accurately and without the IP's intervention, entering at the briefed pitch attitude and holding a constant rate of roll to level flight. Recovery heading was within 6 degrees of the entry heading and recovery airspeed within 7 knots of the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew three consecutive Aileron Rolls with exceptional accuracy, each entered on the same outside reference line and completed on the entry heading. Deviations did not exceed 2 degrees of heading and 3 knots of recovery airspeed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a false attitude perception that was not resolved against the instruments while inverted, did not maintain the briefed pitch attitude through the second half of the Aileron Roll. The A/C completed the roll 35 degrees off the entry heading with recovery airspeed 30 knots above the briefed value, with the result that the IP took control and returned the A/C to level flight. The maneuver was not completed by SP without assistance.

SP, due to rudder input applied against the direction of roll, did not keep the longitudinal axis on the outside reference line through the Aileron Roll. The roll finished 20 degrees off the entry heading with recovery airspeed 15 knots above the briefed value, corrected after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition and correction were delayed.

SP, due to distraction from the primary scan by an unrelated switch action before the entry, did not set the briefed nose position above the horizon before starting the Aileron Roll. Recovery airspeed was 13 knots above the briefed value and the roll finished 14 degrees off the entry heading, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP flew the Aileron Roll accurately and without hesitation, using the outside reference line to hold the longitudinal axis through the roll. Deviations remained inside the desired criteria, with the roll finishing 9 degrees off the entry heading and recovery airspeed 8 knots above the briefed value. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter control of the rate of roll is expected to improve with repetition.

SP flew the Aileron Roll above the desired standard, with smooth and solid control and no pitch deviation through the inverted portion. The roll finished within 2 degrees of the entry heading, with recovery airspeed within 2 knots of the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to failure to recognise the undesired aircraft state before it developed further, did not keep the nose describing a circle around the outside reference point during the Barrel Roll. Bank at the 90 degree point was 30 degrees off the briefed value and the A/C completed the maneuver 32 degrees off the entry heading with recovery airspeed 26 knots above the briefed value, with the result that the IP took control and recovered to level flight.

SP completed the Barrel Roll within the desired standards for the block, controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid way through the inverted position. Bank at the 90 degree point was 20 degrees off the briefed value and recovery airspeed 15 knots above it, corrected after the IP's verbal prompts on each repetition. Marginal performance for the Training Section - self-recognition of the rate of roll deviation is expected to improve.

SP flew the Barrel Roll without verbal prompts or intervention from the IP, holding a near constant G with the nose tracking around the outside reference point. Bank at the inverted position deviated by 14 degrees and recovery airspeed by 12 knots, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner by SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed the Barrel Roll to the standardized procedure with accuracy and speed, keeping the reference point in use throughout the maneuver. The recovery finished within 7 degrees of the entry heading with recovery airspeed within 8 knots of the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Barrel Roll with exceptional accuracy, holding constant G and a symmetrical path of the nose around the outside reference point. The recovery finished within 3 degrees of the entry heading, with bank within 2 degrees of the briefed value at the inverted position. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an insufficient initial pull that did not place the nose above the reference point, did not fly the Barrel Roll with the constant G described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual. The A/C passed the inverted position with the nose low, recovery airspeed reached 30 knots above the briefed value and the recovery finished 30 degrees off the entry heading, with the result that the IP flew the recovery. The Barrel Roll entry technique requires further ground review.

SP, due to situational awareness limited to the instrument in use, without reference to the wider aircraft state, did not track the outside reference point through the second half of the Barrel Roll. Bank at the inverted position was 20 degrees off the briefed value and recovery airspeed 15 knots above the briefed value, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition of the deviation was delayed.

SP flew the Barrel Roll within the desired standards, keeping the nose on a recognizable circular path around the outside reference point. The recovery finished 16 degrees off the entry heading and recovery airspeed reached 13 knots above the briefed value, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency of the constant G through the maneuver is expected to improve.

SP flew the Barrel Roll accurately and promptly without the IP's intervention, entering at the briefed airspeed and tracking the reference point through the inverted position. Recovery airspeed was within 8 knots of the briefed value and the recovery within 6 degrees of the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew consecutive Barrel Rolls with exceptional accuracy, each around the same outside reference point and with constant G throughout. Deviations did not exceed 2 degrees of recovery heading and 3 knots of recovery airspeed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to roll and pull inputs applied at rates that were not matched, did not maintain the constant G required to keep the nose on the circular path around the reference point. The A/C finished the Barrel Roll 35 degrees off the entry heading with recovery airspeed 28 knots above the briefed value, with the result that the IP directed the recovery inputs and returned the A/C to level flight. The maneuver was not completed by SP without assistance.

SP, due to overconfidence in the margin available at that airspeed and bank, entered the Barrel Roll without confirming the entry airspeed against the briefed value. Bank at the 90 degree point was 20 degrees off the briefed value and the recovery finished 20 degrees off the entry heading, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition and correction were delayed.

SP, due to a slightly high rate of roll in the first quadrant, did not keep the nose evenly spaced around the outside reference point through the Barrel Roll. Recovery airspeed was 12 knots above the briefed value and the recovery finished 15 degrees off the entry heading, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP flew the Barrel Roll accurately and without delay, using the outside reference point from entry through the inverted position to the recovery. Deviations remained inside the desired criteria, with the recovery 9 degrees off the entry heading and recovery airspeed 9 knots above the briefed value. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter control of the rate of pull at the entry is expected to improve with repetition.

SP flew the Barrel Roll above the desired standard, with smooth and solid control and no approach to stall at the inverted position. Recovery airspeed was within 2 knots of the briefed value and the recovery within 2 degrees of the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Loop to the block MIF of (0) on the introduction sortie, with the IP setting the entry airspeed and calling the pull and the float over the top. Bank against the reference line was corrected from the front cockpit, which is the expected standard for this stage of the block. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent control of the back pressure through the vertical is expected to improve.

SP flew the Loop to completion on the introduction sortie after the IP's verbal prompts only, with no control input from the front cockpit. Bank over the top was held within 20 degrees of the reference line and the recovery finished 20 degrees off the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Loop without prompting or intervention from the IP, confirming the entry airspeed and holding back pressure through the vertical. Bank over the top reached 15 degrees against the reference line and recovery airspeed 12 knots above the briefed value, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Loop accurately and promptly, floating over the top with the wings checked level against the horizon and no approach to stall. Recovery airspeed was within 7 knots of the briefed value and the recovery within 8 degrees of the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Loop with exceptional precision on the introduction sortie, with a constant rate of pitch change and the wings level over the top. Recovery airspeed was within 2 knots of the briefed value and the recovery within 3 degrees of the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standard entry pull that did not reach the briefed G, did not fly the Loop as the constant radius maneuver described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual. The A/C arrived over the top 22 knots below the briefed minimum airspeed with 30 degrees of bank against the reference line, with the result that the IP took control and completed the maneuver. Further study of the Loop entry parameters is required.

SP completed the Loop within the desired standards for the block, keeping the A/C clear of a stall over the top. The recovery finished 20 degrees off the entry heading with recovery airspeed 15 knots above the briefed value, corrected after the IP's verbal prompts. Marginal performance for the Training Section - recognition of the bank deviation over the top without prompting is expected to improve.

SP flew the Loop without the IP's verbal prompts, following the standardized entry, float and recovery sequence. Bank over the top reached 14 degrees against the reference line and recovery airspeed 13 knots above the briefed value, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner by SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed the Loop to the standardized procedure with accuracy and speed, using the outside reference line and the wingtips to hold the vertical plane. The recovery finished within 6 degrees of the entry heading with recovery airspeed within 8 knots of the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Loop with exceptional accuracy, with a symmetrical profile and smooth, solid control from the entry pull to level flight. Bank over the top was within 2 degrees of the reference line and the recovery within 3 degrees of the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an absent cross-check of aircraft state against the primary flight instruments during the pull, did not confirm the entry airspeed before starting the Loop and did not check the wings level over the top. The recovery finished 32 degrees off the entry heading with recovery airspeed 26 knots above the briefed value, with the result that the IP directed the recovery and flew part of the pull-out.

SP, due to back pressure relaxed in the first quarter of the Loop, did not hold the constant rate of pitch change required for a symmetrical profile. The recovery finished 20 degrees off the entry heading with recovery airspeed 15 knots above the briefed value, corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition of the deviation was delayed.

SP flew the Loop within the desired standards, controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid way from the entry pull to the recovery. Bank over the top reached 17 degrees against the reference line and the recovery finished 14 degrees off the entry heading, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency of the back pressure through the second half is expected to improve.

SP flew the Loop accurately and without the IP's intervention, entering at the briefed airspeed and holding constant back pressure through the vertical. Recovery airspeed was within 8 knots of the briefed value and the recovery within 7 degrees of the entry heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew consecutive Loops with exceptional accuracy, each entered on the same reference line and recovered in the entry plane. Deviations did not exceed 3 degrees of bank over the top and 2 knots of recovery airspeed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to no reset of the maneuver after the first parameter was exceeded, continued the Loop from an entry airspeed 20 knots below the briefed value. The A/C reached the stall buffet over the top with 30 degrees of bank against the reference line, with the result that the IP took control and recovered the A/C. The maneuver was not completed by SP without assistance.

SP, due to an unchecked wing position over the top, did not use the wingtips and the horizon to keep the Loop in the vertical plane. The recovery finished 20 degrees off the entry heading with recovery airspeed 10 knots below the briefed value, corrected after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition and correction were delayed.

SP, due to complacency on a maneuver flown repeatedly without incident, did not confirm the entry airspeed and the reference line before the pull. The A/C floated over the top with 14 degrees of bank against the reference line and the recovery finished 13 degrees off the entry heading, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP flew the Loop accurately and without hesitation, using the wingtips and the horizon to keep the maneuver in the vertical plane. Deviations remained inside the desired criteria, with recovery airspeed 9 knots above the briefed value and the recovery 8 degrees off the entry heading. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more even rate of pitch change over the top is expected to improve with repetition.

SP flew the Loop above the desired standard, with an even rate of pitch change and no approach to stall over the top. The recovery finished within 2 degrees of the entry heading, with recovery airspeed within 3 knots of the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Cuban Eight to the block MIF of (0) on the introduction sortie, with the IP demonstrating the five eighths loop and calling the half roll point on the 45 degree down line. The sequence was completed only with directed inputs from the front cockpit, which is the expected standard at this stage of the block. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent recognition of the 45 degree down line is expected to improve.

SP flew the Cuban Eight to completion on the introduction sortie with the IP's verbal prompts only and no control input from the front cockpit. The half roll finished 20 degrees off the section line with airspeed held within 15 knots of the briefed value. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Cuban Eight without prompting or intervention from the IP, establishing the 45 degree inverted down line before each half roll. Deviations were limited to 14 degrees of heading and 12 knots of airspeed, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Cuban Eight accurately and promptly, with both halves symmetrical about the section line and no approach to stall over either top. Airspeed at the roll points was within 8 knots of the briefed value and the recovery within 7 degrees of the section line. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Cuban Eight with exceptional precision on the introduction sortie, with the half rolls set exactly on the 45 degree down lines. Deviations did not exceed 3 knots of airspeed and 2 degrees of recovery heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an error of omission in the sequence that had been briefed, did not half roll the A/C on the 45 degree down line and continued the inverted descending line past the recovery point of the Cuban Eight. Airspeed at the roll point reached 30 knots above the briefed value and the recovery finished 32 degrees off the section line, with the result that the IP took control and recovered the A/C to level flight.

SP completed the Cuban Eight within the desired standards for the block, keeping the two halves recognizably symmetrical about the section line. The half roll finished 20 degrees off the section line with airspeed 15 knots above the briefed value, corrected after the IP's verbal prompts. Marginal performance for the Training Section - self-recognition of the roll point on the down line is expected to improve.

SP flew the Cuban Eight without the IP's verbal prompts, following the standardized loop, down line and half roll sequence. Airspeed on the down line reached 13 knots above the briefed value and the recovery finished 15 degrees off the section line, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner by SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed the Cuban Eight to the standardized procedure with accuracy and speed, holding the 45 degree down line through each half roll. Recovery airspeed was within 7 knots of the briefed value and the recovery within 8 degrees of the section line. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Cuban Eight with exceptional accuracy, with smooth and solid control through both five eighths loops and no IP prompting at any point. Airspeed at the roll points was within 2 knots of the briefed value and the recovery within 3 degrees of the section line. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an early pull out of the five eighths loop, did not establish the 45 degree inverted down line before the half roll of the Cuban Eight. Recovery airspeed reached 28 knots above the briefed value and the second half was started 30 degrees off the section line, with the result that the IP directed the sequence and flew the second half. Further ground review of the Cuban Eight sequence is required.
